New research released by us today at @isdglobal.bsky.social reveals how false election interference claims in the June 2024 local and European elections in Ireland echo global conspiracy theories, threatening trust ahead of this week’s general election. www.isdglobal.org/isd-publicat...

Our analysis highlights the emergence of false and conspiratorial claims alleging widespread “voter harvesting,” “foreign interference,” and “polling station irregularities” in the June elections mirroring rhetoric from the US Stop the Steal movement.

Allegations of “foreign interference” dominated the claims, often targeting the legal rights of non-citizens to participate in local elections, as well as candidates from migrant backgrounds, and voter engagement by political parties and NGOs. www.isdglobal.org/isd-publicat...

Conspiracy theories alleging that asylum seekers were fast-tracked citizenship in exchange for votes circulated, based on an edited clip originally posted by the Minister for Justice during the pandemic.
Claims of “election rigging” at polling stations and count centres borrowed directly from the language of the US Stop the Steal movement, despite no evidence of systemic issues in Irish elections.

Most of the emphasis for electoral interference claims during the June elections centred on the voting rights of non-citizens in local elections, ISD has since seen a shift to targeting the voting rights of “new citizens” ahead of the general election this Friday. www.isdglobal.org/isd-publicat...

With the regulatory landscape in flux, and legislation meant to curb the spread of mis and disinfo during elections not yet enacted, the ability of the Irish state to push back against threats to electoral integrity and democracy remains dangerously ineffective. www.thejournal.ie/ireland-elec...
